title: Arakhin 13
description: How the Second Temple years and the Jubilees are counted from Ezra’s ascent and from the conquest and division of the land, the six inspected lambs and the Temple’s trumpets, harps and single cymbal, the twelve Levites on the platform and the boys who sang beside them, and, opening the third chapter, the halakhot of valuations that are lenient and stringent.
topics: 🎲 The four watches that returned, Jedaiah first and Jehoiarib subordinate
📅 Rav Ashi: the six years before Ezra came are not counted, and seven years each to conquer and to divide the land
🐑 Six lambs in the Chamber of the Lambs: inspected four days before slaughter, per ben Bag Bag
🎺 Two trumpets up to 120, nine harps and one cymbal
🎶 Twelve Levites on the platform, and the boys who sang “to provide flavor”
🪕 Rabbi Yehuda’s harp of seven, eight and ten strings
📖 Hadran: chapter 2, Ein Ne’erakhin, ends with its lists of minimums
⚖️ Chapter 3 opens: lenient and stringent in valuations, and the gentile in the valuation

a1.he: בָּא חָרִים וְנָטַל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירָיו שֵׁשׁ, וְכֵן פַּשְׁחוּר וְכֵן אִימֵּר. הִתְקִינוּ נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יְהוֹיָרִיב רֹאשׁ מִשְׁמָרוֹת עוֹלֶה — לֹא יִדָּחֶה יְדַעְיָה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, אֶלָּא יְדַעְיָה עִיקָּר וִיהוֹיָרִיב טָפֵל לוֹ, אֶלָּא אַשְּׁאָרָא.

a2.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָנָךְ שֵׁית שְׁנֵי עַד דְּסָלֵיק עֶזְרָא וּמְקַדֵּישׁ לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ,

a3.he: דִּכְתִיב: ״בֵּאדַיִן בְּטֵלַת עֲבִידַת בֵּית אֱלָהָא דִּי בִּירוּשְׁלֶם״, וּכְתִיב: ״וְשֵׁיצִיא בַּיְתָא דְּנָא עַד יוֹם תְּלָתָא לִירַח אֲדָר דְּהִיא שְׁנַת שֵׁית לְמַלְכוּת דָּרְיָוֶשׁ מַלְכָּא״.

a4.he: וְתָנָא: בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן לְשָׁנָה הַבָּאָה עָלָה עֶזְרָא וְגָלוּתוֹ עִמּוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּבֹא יְרוּשָׁלִַם בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁי הִיא הַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִית לַמֶּלֶךְ״.

a5.he: גּוּפָא: שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹבֵלוֹת מָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ לָאָרֶץ וְעַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ, וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ מָנוּ, שֶׁאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ מָנוּ, נִמְצָא בַּיִת חָרֵב בִּתְחִלַּת יוֹבֵל, וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא ״בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״ וְכוּ׳.

a6.he: שֶׁבַע שֶׁכִּיבְּשׁוּ מְנָלַן? דְּקָאָמַר כָּלֵב: ״בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה [אָנֹכִי] בִּשְׁלוֹחַ אוֹתִי מֹשֶׁה עֶבֶד ה׳ מִקָּדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ לְרַגֵּל אֶת הָאָרֶץ, וְעַתָּה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם בֶּן חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁמוֹנִים״.

a7.he: וְאָמַר מָר: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִשְׁכָּן, שְׁנִיָּה הוּקַם הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְשָׁלַח מְרַגְּלִים, כִּי עֲבוּר יַרְדֵּן כָּלֵב בַּר כַּמָּה הָוֵי? בַּר תְּמָנַן נְכֵי תַּרְתֵּין, כִּי קָא מְפַלֵּיג נַחֲלוֹת קָאָמַר: ״בֶּן חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי״, אִישְׁתְּכַח דְּשֶׁבַע כִּיבְּשׁוּ.

a8.he: וְשֶׁבַע שֶׁחִילְּקוּ מְנָלַן? אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִדְּשֶׁבַע כִּיבְּשׁוּ שֶׁבַע חִילְּקוּ, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִדְּלָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ ״אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.

a9.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשִּׁשָּׁה טְלָאִים הַמְבוּקָּרִין בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַטְּלָאִים, כְּדֵי לַשַּׁבָּת וּלְיָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד עוֹלָם. אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת, מִתִּשְׁעָה כִּנּוֹרוֹת, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד עוֹלָם, וְהַצִּלְצָל לְבַד.

a11.he: תַּנָּא בְּעָלְמָא קָאֵי, וְאַתְּמִידִין לְחוֹדֵיהּ קָאֵי, וּמַאי ״כְּדֵי לַשַּׁבָּת וּלְיָמִים טוֹבִים״ — סִימָנָא בְּעָלְמָא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשִּׁשָּׁה טְלָאִים

b1.he: הַמְבוּקָּרִים בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַטְּלָאִים אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה, וּמַנִּי — בֶּן בַּג בַּג הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: בֶּן בַּג בַּג אוֹמֵר, מִנַּיִן לַתָּמִיד שֶׁטָּעוּן בִּיקּוּר אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה?

b2.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״, וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת עַד אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן״, מָה לְהַלָּן טָעוּן בִּיקּוּר אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה, אַף כָּאן טָעוּן בִּיקּוּר אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה.

b3.he: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי ״כְּדֵי לַשַּׁבָּת״, וְלָא קָתָנֵי ״לַשַּׁבָּת״, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b4.he: מִשְּׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת וּמוֹסִיפִין וְכוּ׳. וְעַד כַּמָּה? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב זַבְדִּי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עַד מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְעִמָּהֶם כֹּהֲנִים לְמֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים מַחְצְרִים בַּחֲצוֹצְרוֹת״.

b5.he: מִתִּשְׁעָה כִּנּוֹרוֹת וְכוּ׳ וְצִלְצָל לְבָד. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאָסָף בַּמְצִלְתַּיִם לְהַשְׁמִיעַ״. מְצִלְתַּיִם תְּרֵי הָווּ! כֵּיוָן דַּחֲדָא עֲבִידְתָּא עָבְדִי, וְחַד גַּבְרָא עָבֵיד בְּהוּ — קָרֵי לְהוּ חַד.

b6.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר לְוִיִּם עוֹמְדִין עַל הַדּוּכָן, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד עוֹלָם. אֵין הַקָּטָן נִכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה לַעֲבוֹדָה, אֶלָּא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַלְּוִיִּם אוֹמְרִים בַּשִּׁיר, וְלֹא הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים בְּנֵבֶל וּבְכִנּוֹר, אֶלָּא בַּפֶּה, כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן תֶּבֶל בַּנְּעִימָה.

b7.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: אֵין עוֹלִין לַמִּנְיָן, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לַדּוּכָן, אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ הָיוּ עוֹמְדִין, וְרָאשֵׁיהֶן בֵּין רַגְלֵי הַלְוִיִּם, וְצֹעֲרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הָיוּ נִקְרָאִין.

b8.he: גְּמָ׳ הָנֵי כְּנֶגֶד מִי? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּנֶגֶד תִּשְׁעָה כִּנּוֹרוֹת [וּשְׁנֵי] נְבָלִים וְצִלְצָל אֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוּא וּבָנָיו וְאֶחָיו שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר״.

b9.he: אֵין הַקָּטָן נִכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה לַעֲבוֹדָה אֶלָּא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַלְּוִיִּם כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וַיַּעֲמֹד יֵשׁוּעַ בָּנָיו וְאֶחָיו קַדְמִיאֵל וּבָנָיו בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה כְּאֶחָד לְנַצֵּחַ עַל עֹשֵׂה הַמְּלָאכָה בְּבֵית הָאֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳״.

b10.he: לֹא הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים לֹא בְּנֵבֶל וְלֹא בְּכִנּוֹר, אֶלָּא בַּפֶּה כּוּ׳. לְמֵימְרָא דְּנֵבֶל לְחוּד וְכִנּוֹר לְחוּד? לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כִּנּוֹר שֶׁל מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת נִימִין הָיָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׂבַע שְׂמָחוֹת פָּנֶיךָ״, אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״שׂוֹבַע״ אֶלָּא ״שֶׁבַע״.

b11.he: וְשֶׁל יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ שְׁמוֹנָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִמְנַצֵּחַ עַל הַשְּׁמִינִית״, עַל נִימָא שְׁמִינִית.

b12.he: שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא עֶשֶׂר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עֲלֵי עָשׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי נָבֶל עֲלֵי הִגָּיוֹן בְּכִנּוֹר״.

b13.he: וְאוֹמֵר: ״הוֹדוּ לַה׳ בְּכִנּוֹר בְּנֵבֶל עָשׂוֹר זַמְּרוּ לוֹ שִׁירוּ לוֹ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ״!

b14.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אַיְּידֵי דִּנְפִישִׁי נִימִין דִּידֵיהּ, נְפִישׁ קָלֵיהּ כִּי נֵבֶל, קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״נֵבֶל״.

b15.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: אֵין עוֹלִין מִן הַמִּנְיָן כּוּ׳. תָּנָא: וְסוֹעֲדֵי הַלְוִיִּם הָיוּ נִקְרָאִין. וְתַנָּא דִּידַן? כֵּיוָן דְּהַנֵּי קָטִין קָלַיְיהוּ, וְהָנֵי עָב קָלַיְיהוּ, הָנֵי מְקַטְּטִי וְהָנֵי לָא מְקַטְּטִי, קָרֵי לְהוּ ״צֹעֲרֵי״.

b17.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בַּעֲרָכִין לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר, וּבִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר, וּבְשׁוֹר הַמּוּעָד שֶׁהֵמִית הָעֶבֶד לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר, בָּאוֹנֵס וּבַמְפַתֶּה וּבַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר.

b18.he: יֵשׁ בַּעֲרָכִין לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הַנָּאֶה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶת הַכָּעוּר שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, נוֹתֵן חֲמִשִּׁים סֶלַע, וְאִם אָמַר: ״הֲרֵי דָּמָיו עָלַי״, נוֹתֵן אֶת שׇׁוְויוֹ.

b19.he: גְּמָ׳ יֵשׁ בַּעֲרָכִין לְהָקֵל וְכוּ׳ וּלְהַחְמִיר כֵּיצַד אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ כּוּ׳. בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — אִין, בַּגּוֹיִם — לָא.

b20.he: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דִּתְנַן: גּוֹי, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נֶעֱרָךְ, אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲרִיךְ?

b21.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא

messages.text: Continued from 12b: to show that the baraita equating the two destructions cannot mean every detail, the Gemara noted that the watch of Jehoiarib did not serve in the Second Temple. A baraita taught that only four priestly watches ascended from the Babylonian exile, Jedaiah, Harim, Pashḥur and Immer; the prophets divided them into twenty-four by lot, and Jedaiah drew its own lot and five others, six in all.
Harim came and also drew his portion and the lot of five other watches, for a total of six. And likewise Pashḥur, and likewise Immer.

notes.dh: וכן חרים וכן פשחור וכן אימר
notes.he: ויהויריב שוב לא עלה:
notes.en: And likewise Harim, and likewise Pashḥur, and likewise Immer: and Jehoiarib never again ascended.

messages.text: The prophets among them stipulated that even if the descendants of Jehoiarib, who originally headed the priestly watches, would ascend to Eretz Yisrael, Jedaiah would not be demoted from its place as the first of the watches. Rather, the watch of Jedaiah would retain precedence, and Jehoiarib would be subordinate to it.

notes.he: פרש"י ששוב לא עלה וזהו תימה דמנא ליה ששוב לא עלה דהא משמע שיכול לעלות מדקאמר שאפילו משמרתו של יהויריב עולה ועוד הקשה רבינו אלחנן דהרבה עלו ואין פשוט לנו שלא עלה ואמר רבי דמכל מקום יכול להיות שעלה יהויריב והכא קא פריך הכי משמרתו של יהויריב בשניה מי הואי כי כ"ד היו אלו נגד המשמרות שלא עלו שחלוקות לארבע ועשרים משמרות ושימשו תחתיהם:
notes.en: That even if the watch of Jehoiarib ascends: Rashi explains that he never again ascended. And this is puzzling: from where does he know that he never again ascended? It implies that he could ascend, since it says “that even if the watch of Jehoiarib ascends.” Moreover, Rabbeinu Elḥanan asked: many ascended, and it is not clear to us that he did not ascend. And Rabbi [so the text] said: In any case it is possible that Jehoiarib ascended, and here the Gemara is asking this: was the watch of Jehoiarib [one of the watches] in the Second [Temple]? For the twenty-four were these [four families], corresponding to the watches that did not ascend; they were divided into twenty-four watches and served in their place.

notes.he: יהויריב ראש (משמרה) [משמע דהוא הוה ראש לכל המשמרות] כדכתיב בדברי הימים:
notes.en: Jehoiarib the head [of the watches]: [it implies that he was the head of all the watches], as is written in Chronicles.

messages.text: Rather, when the baraita equates the details pertaining to the destruction of the two Temples, it is referring to other details, i.e., that both were destroyed on the Ninth of Av and on a Sunday, but it is not equating them with regard to all the details.

A third answer to the question about how the baraita can claim that the Second Temple was destroyed in a year following a Sabbatical Year, when a calculation of the number of years that it stood indicates that it was destroyed in a Sabbatical Year:

Those six years from the time the Second Temple was built until Ezra ascended to Eretz Yisrael and sanctified the land are not counted, as the Sabbatical cycle was not in effect during that period. Consequently, the Second Temple was destroyed in a year following a Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: לעולם וכן בשניה אמוצאי שביעית קאי ורבנן היא ודקא קשיא לך לעיל דבשביעית חרוב לא קשיא דשית שני קמאי מבנין הבית עד דסליק עזרא וקידש ארץ ישראל לא מנו שמיטין ויובלות דל שית שנין משני הבית משכחת שנת ת"כ בשביעית כיצד ארבע מאה (ושית שנין) תמניא יובלי וארבע סרי שני תרי שבועי ובשנת תכ"א שהיה מוצאי שביעית חרב:
notes.en: Rav Ashi said: Actually, [“and likewise] in the Second” [Temple] refers to the year after the Sabbatical Year, and it is [in accordance with] the Rabbis. And as for what was difficult for you above, that it was destroyed in a Sabbatical Year, this is not difficult: for the first six years from the building of the House until Ezra ascended and sanctified Eretz Yisrael, they did not count Sabbatical Years and Jubilees. Remove six years from the years of the House, and you find year 420 in a Sabbatical Year. How so? Four hundred [years; the printed text adds “and six years” in parentheses] are eight Jubilees, and fourteen years are two Sabbatical cycles; and in year 421, which was the year after a Sabbatical Year, it was destroyed.

notes.dh: הנך שית עד דסליק עזרא וקדיש לא קחשיב
notes.he: צריך עיון למאי דפירשתי דכי נמי גלו השבטים מנו נמי יובלות כדי לקדש השמיטין א"כ בגלות דבבל קודם דסליק עזרא נמי היו מונין ואמאי התחילו למנות כי סליק עזרא וי"ל דלא דמי דודאי בעוד ישראל על אדמתם כי נמי אין יובל נוהג שמיטה נוהג בחרישה וזריעה והיו מקדשין אבל בגלות לא היו מקדשין כלל שביעית וצ"ע דכי נמי היו בגולה היו צריכין לקדש שביעית מפני שמיטת כספים שנוהגת בין בארץ בין בחוצה לארץ ואם הוא כך דשביעית אינו תלוי ביובל כי נמי ישראל בגלות ואינן כלל על אדמתן למה לא ימנו שמיטין כמו מקצת ישראל על אדמתן ואף על גב דאין כל יושביה עליה מונין שביעית אף על גב שאין מונין יובל:
notes.en: Those six until Ezra ascended and sanctified are not counted: This requires examination according to what I explained, that even when the tribes were exiled they still counted Jubilees in order to sanctify the Sabbatical Years. If so, in the Babylonian exile before Ezra ascended they should also have been counting; why did they begin to count when Ezra ascended? One can say that it is not comparable: certainly while Israel is on its land, even when the Jubilee is not in effect, the Sabbatical Year is in effect with regard to plowing and sowing, and they would sanctify it; but in exile they did not sanctify the Sabbatical Year at all. And this requires examination: even when they were in exile they would need to sanctify the Sabbatical Year because of the remission of debts, which applies both in the land and outside the land. And if it is so that the Sabbatical Year does not depend on the Jubilee, then even when Israel is in exile and not on its land at all, why should they not count Sabbatical cycles, just as when part of Israel is on its land? For even though not all its inhabitants are on it, they count the Sabbatical Year, even though they do not count the Jubilee.

notes.he: [לעולם רבנן ולעולם במוצאי שביעית והא דקשיא דהוה ליה בשיתא בשבוע הא לא קשיא דהנך חמש שני קמייתא דבנו בית שני עד דסליק עזרא וקידש שמיטין ויובלות לא קא חשיב דכתיב באדין בטילת עד תרתין שנין לדריוש דכתיב ושיציא ביתא דנא עד יום תלת לירח אדר דהיא שנת שית למלכות דריוש:
notes.en: [Actually it is the Rabbis, and actually it was destroyed in the year after the Sabbatical Year. And as for the difficulty, that it would be in the sixth [year] of the Sabbatical cycle, that is not difficult: for those first five years in which they built the Second Temple, until Ezra ascended and sanctified Sabbatical Years and Jubilees, are not counted, as it is written: “Then ceased,” until the second year of Darius; as it is written: “And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was the sixth year of the reign of Darius.”

messages.text: It is known that Ezra ascended to Eretz Yisrael six years after the beginning of the construction of the Second Temple, as it is written: “Then ceased the work of the House of God, which is at Jerusalem; and it ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia” (Ezra 4:24). This proves that construction on the Temple started in the second year of the reign of Darius.
messages.quote: Those six years until Ezra ascended

verse.he: בֵּאדַיִן בְּטֵלַת עֲבִידַת בֵּית־אֱלָהָא דִּי בִּירוּשְׁלֶם וַהֲוָת בָּטְלָא עַד שְׁנַת תַּרְתֵּין לְמַלְכוּת דָּרְיָוֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ־פָּרָס׃ {פ}
verse.en: At that time, work on the House of God in Jerusalem stopped and remained in abeyance until the second year of the reign of King Darius of Persia.

notes.dh: ומנלן דעד שית שני לא סליק עזרא דכתיב באדין בטילת וגו'
notes.he: אלמא בשנת שתים לדריוש התחיל הבנין:
notes.en: And from where do we know that Ezra did not ascend until six years [had passed]? As it is written: “Then ceased,” etc. Evidently the building began in the second year of Darius.

messages.text: And it is written: “And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king” (Ezra 6:15), which was the fifth year from when they started building.

verse.he: וְשֵׁיצִיא בַּיְתָה דְנָה עַד יוֹם תְּלָתָה לִירַח אֲדָר דִּי־הִיא שְׁנַת־שֵׁת לְמַלְכוּת דָּרְיָוֶשׁ מַלְכָּא׃ {פ}
verse.en: The house was finished on the third of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.

notes.he: אלמא בשנת שש נשלם הרי חמש שנים ובאותו זמן לשנה הבאה שהיא שנה ששית לבנין עלה עזרא ובא לירושלים בחדש אב ועד תשרי שהוא שבע לבנין לא התחיל למנות:
notes.en: And it is written: “And this house was finished,” etc. Evidently it was completed in year six; that is five years. And at that same time in the following year, which is the sixth year of the building, Ezra ascended and came to Jerusalem in the month of Av; and until Tishrei, which is the seventh [year] of the building, he did not begin to count.

messages.text: At that same time in the following year Ezra ascended from Babylonia together with his company of exiles, as it is written, “And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king” (Ezra 7:8).

verse.he: וַיָּבֹא יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁי הִיא שְׁנַת הַשְּׁבִיעִית לַמֶּלֶךְ׃
verse.en: arriving in Jerusalem in the fifth month in the seventh year of the king.)

notes.he: שהוא שלש (ועשרים) באדר עלה עזרא מבבל ועלה ירושלים בחדש החמישי שאיחר במהלך הדרך מחדש אדר עד חדש אב:
notes.en: At that same time in the following year: which is the third [the text adds “and twentieth” in parentheses] of Adar, Ezra ascended from Babylonia, and he arrived at Jerusalem in the fifth month, for he was delayed on the journey from the month of Adar until the month of Av.

notes.he: ואותו זמן לשנה הבאה עלה עזרא מבבל אלמא שית שנין הוה דלא סליק עזרא וכתיב ויבא ירושלים בחדש החמישי היא שנת שביעית למלך מלמד שמשביעית ואילך התחיל לקדש:
notes.en: And at that same time in the following year Ezra ascended from Babylonia: evidently there were six years in which Ezra did not ascend. And it is written: “And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was the seventh year of the king.” This teaches that from the seventh [year] onward he began to sanctify.

messages.text: Accordingly, Ezra came to Eretz Yisrael six years after the beginning of the construction of the Temple. It was at that time that the counting of the Sabbatical and Jubilee cycles began. The counting continued for 414 years until the destruction of the Temple, which means that the Temple was destroyed in a Sabbatical Year.
§ The Gemara discusses the matter itself that is taught in the baraita cited earlier (12b):
The Jewish people counted seventeen Jubilees from when they entered Eretz Yisrael until they left when the Temple was destroyed.

And you cannot say that they counted from when they entered, because if you say they counted from when they entered, the result is that the Temple was destroyed at the beginning of the Jubilee cycle, and you do not find that the Jubilee Year was “in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten” (Ezekiel 40:1). Rather, remove from them the seven years when they conquered Eretz Yisrael and the seven years when they divided Eretz Yisrael, as the first Jubilee cycle began after the Jewish people conquered and divided Eretz Yisrael.

verse.he: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה לְגָלוּתֵנוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר בְּעֶצֶם ׀ הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה הָיְתָה עָלַי יַד־יְהֹוָה וַיָּבֵא אֹתִי שָׁמָּה׃
verse.en: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the fourteenth year after the city had fallen, at the beginning of the year, the tenth day of the month—on that very day—GOD’s hand came upon me, and it brought me there.

messages.text: From where do we derive that there were seven years during which the Jewish people conquered Eretz Yisrael?
messages.quote: counted seventeen Jubilees from when they entered

messages.text: As Caleb said to Joshua, when it came time to divide Eretz Yisrael at the conclusion of part of the conquest: “Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land…and now, behold, I am this day eighty-five years old” (Joshua 14:7, 10).

verse.he: בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי בִּשְׁלֹחַ מֹשֶׁה עֶבֶד־יְהֹוָה אֹתִי מִקָּדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ לְרַגֵּל אֶת־הָאָרֶץ וָאָשֵׁב אֹתוֹ דָּבָר כַּאֲשֶׁר עִם־לְבָבִי׃ וְאַחַי אֲשֶׁר עָלוּ עִמִּי הִמְסִיו אֶת־לֵב הָעָם וְאָנֹכִי מִלֵּאתִי אַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָי׃ וַיִּשָּׁבַע מֹשֶׁה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמֹר אִם־לֹא הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר דָּרְכָה רַגְלְךָ בָּהּ לְךָ תִהְיֶה לְנַחֲלָה וּלְבָנֶיךָ עַד־עוֹלָם כִּי מִלֵּאתָ אַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָי׃ וְעַתָּה הִנֵּה הֶחֱיָה יְהֹוָה ׀ אוֹתִי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר זֶה אַרְבָּעִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה מֵאָז דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֶת־הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה אֲשֶׁר־הָלַךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר וְעַתָּה הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם בֶּן־חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה׃
verse.en: I was forty years old when Moses the servant of GOD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I gave him a forthright report. While my companions who went up with me took the heart out of the people, I was loyal to my ETERNAL God. On that day, Moses promised on oath, ‘The land on which your foot trod shall be a portion for you and your descendants forever, because you were loyal to my ETERNAL God.’ Now GOD has preserved me, just as promised. It is forty-five years since GOD made this promise to Moses, when Israel was journeying through the wilderness; and here I am today, eighty-five years old.

messages.text: During the first year after the exodus, Moses constructed the Tabernacle; during the second year, the Tabernacle was erected and Moses sent the spies.
Consequently, how old was Caleb when the Jewish people crossed the Jordan? He was eighty less two, i.e., seventy-eight years old.

notes.he: דמשילוח מרגלים עד שנכנסו לארץ אינו אלא ל"ח לבד משנת השילוח דהא בשניה ליציאת מצרים נשתלחו:
notes.en: Eighty less two: for from the sending of the spies until they entered the land was only thirty-eight [years], apart from the year of the sending, since they were sent in the second [year] after the exodus from Egypt.

notes.dh: כלב כמה הוי בר תמנין נכי תרתין
notes.he: והקשה רבינו אלחנן והא מנין לנו שבשנה שניה דווקא היה כלב בן מ' שנה דאז הוה כי עבר ישראל את הירדן בר תמנין נכי תרין שמא התחיל שנת הארבעים ואחד שלו ובשילוח מרגלים היה בסוף הארבעים שהרי שנות כלב לא מצינו וכשעברו ישראל את הירדן הוה בר תמנין נכי חד ומנא להש"ס הא דז' כיבשו וז' חילקו ואמר רבי דלא בא הכתוב לסתום אלא לפרש דמה לנו לשנות כלב אם לא להודיענו בודאי שז' כיבשו וז' חילקו:
notes.en: How old was Caleb? Eighty less two: Rabbeinu Elḥanan asked: from where do we know that Caleb was forty years old precisely in the second year, so that when Israel crossed the Jordan he was eighty less two? Perhaps he had begun his forty-first year, and at the sending of the spies he was at the end of his fortieth, for we do not find Caleb’s years [stated]; and then when Israel crossed the Jordan he was eighty less one. So from where does the Talmud know that they conquered for seven and divided for seven? And Rabbi [so the text] said: The verse does not come to obscure but to explain; for why do we need Caleb’s years, if not to inform us with certainty that they conquered for seven and divided for seven?

notes.he: כי עברו ישראל הירדן לסוף מ' שנה שהיו במדבר הוה כלב בן ע"ח שנים:
notes.en: When Israel crossed the Jordan, at the end of the forty years that they were in the wilderness, Caleb was seventy-eight years old.

messages.text: When Joshua was dividing Eretz Yisrael into inheritances, Caleb said to him: I am eighty-five years old. It is therefore found that they conquered the land for seven years.
And from where do we derive that there were seven years during which the Jewish people divided up Eretz Yisrael into ancestral portions?
messages.quote: seven years during which the Jewish people conquered

messages.text: If you wish, say that from the fact that they conquered the land for seven years, it is reasonable to assume that they divided the land for seven years.

And if you wish, say instead: It can be derived from the fact that you do not find that “the fourteenth year after the city was smitten” (Ezekiel 40:1) was a Jubilee Year (see 12a) unless the Jewish people divided Eretz Yisrael for seven years.

notes.dh: מדלא משכחת ארבע עשרה שנה אחרי אשר הוכתה העיר
notes.he: דליהוי יובל אי לא מדלית ארבע עשרה לכיבוש ולחילוק:
notes.en: From the fact that you do not find “fourteen years after the city was smitten”: that it should be a Jubilee, unless you subtract fourteen for the conquest and the division.

notes.he: (מונה) אחרי שהוכתה העיר יובל אלא א"כ חשבת נמי ז' שחילקו]:
notes.en: From the fact that you do not find fourteen years after the city was smitten [to be a] Jubilee, unless you also count the seven years in which they divided.]

messages.text: Mishna

One maintains no fewer than six lambs that have been inspected for blemishes in the Chamber of the Lambs, which are sufficient for the offerings of Shabbat and for the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana that may occur adjacent to it. And one may add inspected lambs up to an infinite number.

notes.he: ממום:
notes.en: That are inspected: for a blemish.

notes.he: כדי לשבת ולשני ימים טובים:
notes.en: Sufficient for Shabbat and for the two Festival days.

messages.text: One plays no fewer than two trumpets and no fewer than nine harps in the Temple, and one may add up to an infinite number.

notes.he: לא אתפרש טעמא:
notes.en: Mishna. Than nine harps: the reason is not explained.

messages.text: And the cymbal was played alone, and none may be added to it.

notes.he: צלצל אחד היה שם ולא יותר וטעמא מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: And the cymbal alone: there was one cymbal there and no more, and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara

The Gemara assumes that the mishna means that there must be at least six inspected lambs in the Chamber of the Lambs, so that if Rosh HaShana occurs on the two days adjacent to Shabbat, there will be enough lambs available for all the communal offerings that are sacrificed on those days. But there are more than six lambs which are required for the daily offerings and additional offerings of a Shabbat and Rosh HaShana that are adjacent to one another, as one day of Rosh HaShana alone requires sixteen lambs.
messages.quote: sufficient for Shabbat and for the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana

notes.he: גמ' קס"ד כדי לשבת ולשני ימים טובים דווקא קאמר דלהכי בעינן ששה שאם יבאו יחד שבת ושני ימים טובים של ראש השנה ולא יוכלו לבקר יהו להם אילים מזומנים:
notes.en: Gemara. It enters our mind [at first] that he says “sufficient for Shabbat and for the two Festival days” precisely: that for this reason we require six, so that if Shabbat and the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana come together and they cannot inspect, they will have [lambs] ready [Rashi’s word is “rams”].

notes.he: טובא הוי לצורך שבת ולשני ימים טובים של ר"ה צריכין טלאין הרבה לצורך תמידין ומוספין ואינו די בששה:
notes.en: There are many: for Shabbat and the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana many lambs are needed for the daily offerings and additional offerings, and six do not suffice.

messages.text: The tanna is referring to the general policy for the entire year, and he is referring only to the number of lambs necessary for the daily offerings sacrificed over the course of three ordinary days.

notes.he: דבכל ימות השנה נמי בעינן ששה ולאו משום שבת וראש השנה אלא משום דבן בג בג וכדמפרש בסמוך:
notes.en: Refers to the general case: that on all the days of the year as well we require six, and not because of Shabbat and Rosh HaShana, but because of ben Bag Bag, as is explained shortly.

messages.text: And what is the meaning of the phrase: Sufficient for Shabbat and for the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana? It is merely a mnemonic device, and this is what he is saying: One maintains no fewer than six lambs

notes.he: שלא תטעה בגירסא שלא תשנה ארבעה או חמשה משום הכי נקט הנך שלשה ימים דבעו ששה תמידין:
notes.en: Merely a mnemonic: so that you do not err in the wording and teach four or five; for this reason he mentioned these three days, which require six daily offerings.

notes.he: הכא מפרש מעיקרא דכדי לשבת סימנא בעלמא אבל במנחות פרק התכלת (מנחות דף מט: ושם) לא אמר הכי עד דבמסקנא דקאמר התם אמר רבינא לרב אשי הני ששה שבעה הוו דהא איכא צפרא דחד בשבתא דווקא נקט לשבת וה"פ אם היו ב' ימים ראש השנה ביום החמישי וביום ששי ביום הראשון יבקרו התמיד שהוא ארבעה ימים קודם שחיטתו של ה' בשבת ושל יום ו' שהוא שני לר"ה יבקרו ביום שני שהוא ד' ימים קודם שחיטתו וכן של שבת מבקרו ביום ג' ופריך שבעה הוו דהא איכא צפרא דחד בשבתא שגם הוא טעון ביקור ד' ימים קודם שחיטתו וא"כ היאך יפחתו מז':
notes.en: What is “sufficient for Shabbat”? Merely a mnemonic: Here it explains from the outset that “sufficient for Shabbat” is merely a mnemonic. But in Menaḥot, chapter HaTekhelet (Menaḥot 49b), it does not say so until the conclusion, where it says: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: These six are seven, for there is the morning of Sunday. [There] it mentioned Shabbat precisely, and this is the explanation: if the two days of Rosh HaShana were on Thursday and Friday, on Sunday they would inspect the daily offering of Thursday, which is four days before its slaughter; and that of Friday, which is the second [day] of Rosh HaShana, they would inspect on Monday, which is four days before its slaughter; and likewise that of Shabbat is inspected on Tuesday. And he asks: they are seven, for there is the morning of Sunday, which also requires inspection four days before its slaughter; and if so, how can they have fewer than seven?

messages.text: that have been inspected in the Chamber of the Lambs for four days prior to the time of their slaughter. The reserve of six lambs ensured that each lamb would be available for inspection for three days prior to the day of its sacrifice, for a total of four.

notes.he: ומשום הכי בעינן ששה לעולם דבשעת חינוך נתנו שם ששה מבוקרין ד' ימים קודם לכן ונטלו יום ראשון שנים לתמידים ונתנו שנים תחתיהם ויבקרום ביום שני נטלו שנים מן הארבעה הנותרים ונתנו שנים תחתיהם ויום שלישי נטלו שנים הנותרים מן הראשונים ונתנו שנים תחתיהן וכן לעולם נוטלים שנים ונותנים שנים ואותן שנתבקרו וניתנו שם יום ראשון ראויים ליום רביעי ואותן שניתנו בשני ראויין בחמישי וכן חוזרין חלילה לעולם ונמצאו כל התמידין הנשחטין מבוקרין ד' ימים קודם שחיטה עם יום הביקור ויום השחיטה כך שמעתי. וקשיא לי הא לא דמי לארבעה ימים דפסח דביקורו בעשור ושחיטתו בי"ד הרי ארבעה ימים לבד מיום השחיטה ולכך נראה בעיני דשמונה ניתנו שם ביום חינוך וששה דקתני במתני' הכי משמע אין פוחתים מששה כלומר שאפילו כשיטלו השנים שבכל יום נשתיירו שם ששה מבוקרין ולאחר כך קודם הלילה יבקרו שנים ויתנו שם והנך הואיל וליתנהו אכתי בשעת נטילת השנים לא קחשיב להו. ל"א סימנא בעלמא דכי היכי דכי מקלעי שבת ור"ה גבי הדדי מיבקר ההוא דשלישי בשבת בע"ש דהא לא מצו היום לילך ולבקש טלה ולבקרו השתא הוי ארבעה ימים קודם שחיטה הכי נמי לעולם בעינן ד' ימים קודם שחיטה:
notes.en: Four days before slaughter: and for this reason we always require six. At the time of inauguration they placed there six [lambs] inspected four days before. On the first day they took two for the daily offerings and put two in their place, and inspected them; on the second day they took two of the remaining four and put two in their place; and on the third day they took the two that remained of the first ones and put two in their place. And so always they take two and put two; and those that were inspected and placed there on the first day are fit for the fourth day, and those placed on the second are fit for the fifth, and so they go around forever. Thus all the daily offerings that are slaughtered are inspected four days before slaughter, counting the day of inspection and the day of slaughter. So I heard. But it is difficult for me: this is not comparable to the four days of the Paschal offering, whose inspection is on the tenth and its slaughter on the fourteenth, which is four days apart from the day of slaughter. Therefore it seems to me that eight were placed there on the day of inauguration, and the “six” taught in the mishna means this: one does not have fewer than six; that is, even when they take the two of each day, six inspected ones remain there. And afterward, before nightfall, they inspect two and place them there; and those, since they are not yet there at the time the two are taken, are not counted. Another version: merely a mnemonic: just as when Shabbat and Rosh HaShana fall next to each other, the [lamb] for Tuesday is inspected on Friday, since on those days they cannot go and seek out a lamb and inspect it, so that it is then four days before slaughter, so too we always require four days before slaughter.

notes.he: בעלמא קאי אימות החול ואתמידין לחודייהו קאמר והאי דקאמר כדי לשבת ולב' יו"ט לסימנא בעלמא שצריכין להיות ששה תמידין [מבוקרין בכל יום בלישכה מ"ט כדי שישחטו בכל יום של שבוע ב' תמידין] שיהיו מבוקרין ד' ימים קודם שחיטה הא כיצד היו לה ביום ראשון ששה מבוקרין שחט ב' מהן ביום ראשון והביא ב' תחתיהן נשתיירו ד' מבוקרין וב' שאין מבוקרין הרי ו' וביום ב' ישחט ב' מן המבוקרין ויביא ב' אחרים תחתיהן [וביום ג' ישחט ב' מבוקרים ויביא ב' אחרים תחתיהן] אותן שהביא ביום ראשון תחת אותן ששחט יהו ראויין להקריב ביום רביעי שהרי הן מבוקרין ד' ימים ומקצת יום ד' הוי ככולו ואותן שהביא ביום ב' ראויין ליום ה' ושל יום ג' ליום ו' ושל יום ד' לשבת [ושל יום ה' ליום א'] וכך חוזר חלילה והוי בכל יום ב' מבוקרין הלכך אין פוחתים בלשכה מששה טלאים המבוקרים:
notes.en: Refers to the general case: to ordinary weekdays, and he refers to the daily offerings alone. And what he says, “sufficient for Shabbat and for the two Festival days,” is merely a mnemonic, that there must be six daily-offering lambs [inspected every day in the chamber. What is the reason? So that on each day of the week they may slaughter two daily offerings] that were inspected four days before slaughter. How so? On the first day [of the week] there were six inspected; he slaughtered two of them on the first day and brought two in their place; there remained four inspected and two not inspected, which makes six. On the second day he slaughters two of the inspected and brings two others in their place; [on the third day he slaughters two inspected and brings two others in their place.] Those he brought on the first day in place of those he slaughtered are fit to be offered on the fourth day, for they have been inspected four days, and part of the fourth day is like all of it; and those he brought on the second day are fit for the fifth day, and those of the third day for the sixth, and those of the fourth day for Shabbat, [and those of the fifth day for the first day,] and so it goes around; and every day there are two inspected [for slaughter]. Therefore one has no fewer than six inspected lambs in the chamber.

messages.caption: Six lambs in the chamber: each day two are offered and two newly inspected lambs take their place, so that every lamb is inspected four days before its slaughter (as Rabbeinu Gershom, and the explanation Rashi heard, lay it out).

messages.text: And whose opinion is this? It is the opinion of ben Bag Bag, as it is taught in a baraita:
From where is it derived that the daily offering requires examination four days prior to its slaughter?

The verse states with regard to the daily offering: “My food that is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a pleasing aroma unto Me, shall you safeguard to offer unto Me in its due season” (Numbers 28:2);

verse.he: צַו אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אֶת־קׇרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי רֵיחַ נִיחֹחִי תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ׃
verse.en: Command the Israelite people and say to them: Be punctilious in presenting to Me at stated times the offerings of food due Me, as offerings by fire of pleasing odor to Me.

messages.text: and it states there, with regard to the Paschal offering: “In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb…and it shall be for you as a safeguard until the fourteenth day of this month” (Exodus 12:3–6), i.e., the first month.

verse.he: דַּבְּרוּ אֶל־כׇּל־עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר בֶּעָשֹׂר לַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה וְיִקְחוּ לָהֶם אִישׁ שֶׂה לְבֵית־אָבֹת שֶׂה לַבָּיִת׃ וְאִם־יִמְעַט הַבַּיִת מִהְיוֹת מִשֶּׂה וְלָקַח הוּא וּשְׁכֵנוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ בְּמִכְסַת נְפָשֹׁת אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּׂה׃ שֶׂה תָמִים זָכָר בֶּן־שָׁנָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם מִן־הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן־הָעִזִּים תִּקָּחוּ׃ וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת עַד אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה וְשָׁחֲטוּ אֹתוֹ כֹּל קְהַל עֲדַת־יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם׃
verse.en: Speak to the whole community of Israel and say that on the tenth of this month each family shall take for itself a lamb, means either “sheep” or “goat”; cf. v. 5. a lamb to a household. But if the household is too small for a lamb, let it share one with a neighbor who dwells nearby, in proportion to the number of persons: you shall contribute for the lamb according to what each household will eat. Your lamb shall be without blemish, a yearling male; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats. You shall keep watch over it until the fourteenth day of this month; and all the assembled congregation of the Israelites shall slaughter it at twilight.

messages.text: Since the word “safeguard” appears in both verses, it is derived that just as in the verse there, the Paschal offering requires examination four days prior to its slaughter, so too here, the daily offering requires examination four days prior to its slaughter.

The language of the mishna is also precise, according to the explanation that the mishna is referring to Shabbat and Rosh HaShana merely as a mnemonic device, as it teaches that the six lambs are sufficient for Shabbat and the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana, and it does not teach that the six lambs are for use on Shabbat and the two days of Rosh HaShana. Learn from the language of the mishna that this explanation is correct.

notes.he: דסימנא בעלמא הוא ולאו משום טעמא דשבת וראש השנה קא בעי להו מדלא קתני לשבת ולשני ימים כו' דהוי משמע לצורך שבת ור"ה מדקתני כדי ש"מ כפי חשבון הראוי לשבת ולראש השנה דהיינו ששה וסימנא בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: It is also precise: that it is merely a mnemonic, and that he does not require them because of Shabbat and Rosh HaShana: since it does not teach “for Shabbat and for the two days,” etc., which would imply for the needs of Shabbat and Rosh HaShana. Since it teaches “sufficient,” learn from it [that it means] according to the count appropriate for Shabbat and Rosh HaShana, which is six, and it is merely a mnemonic.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that one plays no fewer than two trumpets, and one may add to that number. Until how many trumpets may these additions be made?

notes.dh: ומוסיפין עד עולם עד כמה אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה כו'
notes.he: ואמר רבי דהא ודאי פשיטא שיוכלו להוסיף עד העולם אלא בעי עד כמה יהא הידור מצוה וא"צ לחפש יותר אחר כהנים אמר רב הונא עד ק"כ דהא אשכחן בקרא (דברי הימים ב ה) שחפשו אחרי ק"כ כהנים לתקוע בחצוצרות ולא יותר אי נמי דהא פשיטא דאין מוסיפין עד העולם שאם יוסיפו יותר עירבוב קלא אמר רב הונא עד ק"כ כהנים יכול להוסיף דהא אשכחנא בקרא דלא חיישינן לעירבוב קלא:
notes.en: And one may add up to an infinite number; until how many? Rav Huna said, and some say, etc.: And Rabbi [so the text] said: It is certainly obvious that one may add infinitely. Rather, he asks: until how many is it an enhancement of the mitzva, so that one need not search further for priests? Rav Huna said: Up to 120, for we find in the verse (II Chronicles 5) that they sought out 120 priests to blow trumpets, and no more. Alternatively: it is obvious that one does not add infinitely, for if they added more there would be a jumble of sound. Rav Huna said: One may add up to 120 priests, for we find in the verse that we are not concerned about a jumble of sound [with that many].

messages.alt: and some say Rav Zavdi says that Rav Huna says
messages.text: They may play up to 120 trumpets, as it is stated: “And with them one hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets” (II Chronicles 5:12).

verse.he: וְהַלְוִיִּם הַמְשֹׁרְרִים לְכֻלָּם לְאָסָף לְהֵימָן לִידֻתוּן וְלִבְנֵיהֶם וְלַאֲחֵיהֶם מְלֻבָּשִׁים בּוּץ בִּמְצִלְתַּיִם וּבִנְבָלִים וְכִנֹּרוֹת עֹמְדִים מִזְרָח לַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְעִמָּהֶם כֹּהֲנִים לְמֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים (מחצררים) [מַחְצְרִים] בַּחֲצֹצְרוֹת׃
verse.en: all the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, their sons and their brothers, dressed in fine linen, holding cymbals, harps, and lyres, were standing to the east of the altar, and with them were 120 priests who blew trumpets.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that one plays no fewer than nine harps and one may add up to an infinite number, and the cymbal was played alone and none may be added to it. From where is this matter derived?
messages.quote: And the cymbal was played alone

notes.he: דצלצל לבד ותו לא:
notes.en: From where is this matter derived: that there is a cymbal alone and no more.

messages.text: It is that which the verse states: “And Asaph with the cymbals, sounding aloud” (I Chronicles 16:5), which indicates that only one Levite played the cymbals.

verse.he: אָסָף הָרֹאשׁ וּמִשְׁנֵהוּ זְכַרְיָה יְעִיאֵל וּשְׁמִירָמוֹת וִיחִיאֵל וּמַתִּתְיָה וֶאֱלִיאָב וּבְנָיָהוּ וְעֹבֵד אֱדֹם וִיעִיאֵל בִּכְלֵי נְבָלִים וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת וְאָסָף בַּמְצִלְתַּיִם מַשְׁמִיעַ׃
verse.en: Asaph the chief, Zechariah second in rank, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres, and Asaph sounding the cymbals,

notes.he: שם הלוי:
notes.en: And Asaph: the name of the Levite.

notes.he: במצלתים היינו צלצל:
notes.en: With the cymbals [metziltayim]: this is the cymbal [tziltzal].

messages.text: The word cymbals is in the plural, indicating that there were two; why, then, does the mishna say that there is only one cymbal?
Since two cymbals perform one act and one person plays them by banging them together, the mishna calls them one instrument.

notes.he: דאין אחד מועיל בלא חבירו שהן ב' חתיכות רחבות של מתכת ומכין זו על זו וקורין צינב"ש:
notes.en: They perform one act: for one is of no use without its fellow; they are two broad pieces of metal, and one strikes them against each other (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: [כיון דחדא עיבידתא עבדי וחד גברא שמכה זה בזה קרו להו חד צלצל]:
notes.en: [Since they perform one act, and one man strikes one against the other, they call them one cymbal.]

messages.text: Mishna
In the Temple, there are no fewer than twelve Levites standing on the platform adjacent to the altar and singing, and one may add Levites on the platform up to an infinite number.

notes.dh: [אין] פוחתין מי"ב לוים העומדין על הדוכן
notes.he: בכל יום כשאומרים שירה שנים לנבלים וט' כינורות וצלצל הרי י"ב ושתי חצוצרות כהנים תוקעים בהן ולא לוים והכי תנן פרק בתרא דתמיד (דף לג:) ושני כהנים עומדים על שולחן החלבים וב' חצוצרות בידם ולא חש התם למתני כינורים וחלילים לפי שלא היו בכהנים אלא בלוים וק"ק דקתני התם והקיש בן ארזא בצילצל ותירץ דחדא מינייהו נקט:
notes.en: No fewer than twelve Levites standing on the platform: every day when they say the song: two lyres and nine harps and a cymbal, that makes twelve. And the two trumpets: priests blow them, and not Levites. And so we learned in the last chapter of Tamid (33b): “And two priests stand at the table of the fats with two trumpets in their hands.” And there it did not bother to teach the harps and the flutes, because they were played not by priests but by Levites. And it is slightly difficult, since it teaches there: “And ben Arza struck the cymbal.” And he answered that it mentioned one of them.

messages.text: A minor Levite may enter the Temple courtyard for service only at a time when the Levites are engaging in song, so that he may accompany them.

notes.he: לוי קטן נכנס לעזרה לשום עבודה כגון לכבד את העזרה ולהגיף את הדלתות אלא בשעה שהלוים עומדים על הדוכן בשיר אז נכנסים לוים קטנים לשורר עמהן:
notes.en: Mishna. A minor Levite does not enter the courtyard for any service, such as sweeping the courtyard and closing the doors, except at the time when the Levites stand on the platform in song; then minor Levites enter to sing with them.

notes.he: בן לוי:
notes.en: A minor does not: [enter], a Levite.

notes.he: לשיר:
notes.en: Enter the courtyard for service: for song.

notes.he: הגדולים עומדין [בשיר] שהיו קטני הלוים נכנסין לסייע את הלוים בשיר:
notes.en: Except at the time when the Levites: the adults stand [in song], for the minor Levites would enter to assist the Levites in the song.

messages.text: And minors would not engage in playing a lyre and in playing a harp; rather, they would engage in singing with the mouth, in order to provide flavor to the music with their pure, high voices.

notes.he: אותן קטנים:
notes.en: And they would not: those minors.

notes.dh: אומרים בנבל וכנור אלא בפה ליתן תבל בנעימה
notes.he: ליתן תבלין בנעימות הלוים לפי שקול הלוים הקטנים דק ומתבל את קול הלוים הגדולים:
notes.en: Say with a lyre and a harp, but with the mouth, in order to provide flavor to the music: to put spice into the pleasantness of the Levites, because the voice of the minor Levites is fine and it seasons the voice of the adult Levites.

notes.he: ולא היו אומרים אותן תינוקות השירה:
notes.en: And those children would not say the song:

notes.he: לא בנבל ולא בכנור אלא בפה כדי ליתן תבל בנעימה כלומר לפי שקול הילדים הוא דק היה קולן מנעים את השירה כמו תבלין המנעימין את המאכל:
notes.en: Not with a lyre and not with a harp, but with the mouth, in order to provide flavor to the music: that is, because the voice of the children is fine, their voice would make the song pleasant, like spices that make food pleasant.

messages.text: Minors are not tallied in the minimum total of twelve Levites, and they do not ascend to the platform; rather, they would stand on the ground and their heads would reach to between the legs of the Levites, and they were called cadets [tzoarei] of the Levites.

notes.he: דלא מנו אותן לוים למנין שנים עשר לוים הצריכין לדוכן:
notes.en: [And they are not tallied in the count]: that those Levites are not counted in the count of twelve Levites needed for the platform.

notes.he: על האצטבא המוכנת לדוכן אלא בארץ היו עומדין:
notes.en: And they do not ascend: onto the bench prepared for the platform; rather, they would stand on the ground.

notes.he: שמצערין את הלוים כדמפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: And cadets [tzoarei] of the Levites: for they cause the Levites anguish [metza’arin], as is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: [אין עולין למנין אותו תינוק אין עולה למנין י"ב לוים:
notes.en: [They are not tallied in the count: that child is not tallied in the count of twelve Levites.

notes.he: ולא עומדין בדוכן באותו מקום גבוה שהלוים עומדין שם:
notes.en: And they do not stand on the platform: in that high place where the Levites stand.

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna states that a minimum of twelve Levites would stand on the platform and sing. To what does this number correspond?
messages.quote: no fewer than twelve Levites standing on the platform

messages.text: It corresponds to the minimum number of instruments that were played: Nine harps and two lyres and one cymbal.

notes.he: שנאמר הוא ואחיו ובניו שנים עשר שחילקו הלויים לכ"ד משמרות כנגד כ"ד משמרות כהונה והגיע לכל משמר י"ב כדכתיב בדברי הימים בכל אחד הוא ואחיו ובניו שנים עשר וכשתצרף כולם יבא לכל משמר שנים עשר:
notes.en: As it is stated: “he and his brethren and sons were twelve”: for the Levites were divided into twenty-four watches, corresponding to the twenty-four priestly watches, and each watch received twelve, as is written in Chronicles of each one: “he and his brethren and sons were twelve.” And when you combine them all, each watch comes to twelve.

messages.text: This number is also alluded to in the Bible, as it is stated: “Instructed in singing unto the Lord…he and his brethren and sons were twelve” (I Chronicles 25:7–9).

verse.he: וַיֵּצֵא הַגּוֹרָל הָרִאשׁוֹן לְאָסָף לְיוֹסֵף {ס}        גְּדַלְיָהוּ הַשֵּׁנִי הוּא־וְאֶחָיו וּבָנָיו שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר׃ {ס}
verse.en: The first lot fell to Asaph—to Joseph; the second, to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and his sons—12;

messages.caption: The Temple’s minimum ensemble in this chapter’s mishnayot, with Rav Pappa’s count of the twelve Levites.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: A minor Levite may enter the Temple courtyard for service only at a time when the Levites are engaging in song. From where is this matter derived?
messages.quote: A minor Levite may enter the Temple courtyard for service only at a time when the Levites are engaging in song

messages.text: As the verse states: “Then stood Jeshua with his sons and his brethren, and Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to make music for the workmen in the House of God” (Ezra 3:9). This verse shows that in making music it is preferable to have one’s sons, i.e., minors, as accompaniment.

verse.he: וַיַּעֲמֹד יֵשׁוּעַ בָּנָיו וְאֶחָיו קַדְמִיאֵל וּבָנָיו בְּנֵי־יְהוּדָה כְּאֶחָד לְנַצֵּחַ עַל־עֹשֵׂה הַמְּלָאכָה בְּבֵית הָאֱלֹהִים {ס}        בְּנֵי חֵנָדָד בְּנֵיהֶם וַאֲחֵיהֶם הַלְוִיִּם׃
verse.en: Jeshua, his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together were appointed in charge of those who did the work in the House of God; also the sons of Henadad, their sons and their Levite kin.

notes.dh: אין קטן נכנס בעזרה מנה"מ אמר ר' יוחנן [דאמר קרא] ויעמוד ישוע בניו ואחיו קדמיאל
notes.he: והקשה רבינו אלחנן היכי ילפינן דקטן נכנס לעזרה לשיר בשעה שהלוים עומדים לדוכן ואמר ר"י דרבי ליה מיתורא דקרא כתיב בניהם ואחיהם הלוים וכתיב ישוע בניו קדמיאל ובניו בני יהודה בני (מורד) [חנדד] בניהם למה לי והלא הזכיר כל אחד בניו אלא ש"מ דלהכי כתביה דהוה מיותר ומשמע קטנים:
notes.en: A minor does not enter the courtyard; from where is this matter derived? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: As the verse states: “Then stood Jeshua, his sons and his brethren, Kadmiel”: Rabbeinu Elḥanan asked: How do we derive that a minor enters the courtyard for song at a time when the Levites stand on the platform? And Ri said that he includes it from a superfluity in the verse. It is written: “their sons and their brethren the Levites,” and it is written: “Jeshua, his sons…Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, the sons of Ḥenadad” [the printed text reads “Morad,” corrected in brackets to “Ḥenadad”]. Why do I need “their sons”? Hasn’t it already mentioned each one’s sons? Rather, learn from it that it was written for this, since it is superfluous, and it implies minors.

notes.he: ובני יהודה היו קטנים מלמד שכולן מנצחין בשיר גדולים וקטנים:
notes.en: As it is stated: “his sons”; and the sons of Judah were minors. This teaches that all of them led in song, adults and minors.

messages.text: That is to say that a lyre and a harp are two distinct instruments. Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: would not engage in playing a lyre and in playing a harp; rather, they would engage in singing with the mouth

messages.text: The harp used in the Temple was an instrument of seven strings, as it is stated: “In your presence is fullness [sova] of joy, in your right hand sweetness for evermore” (Psalms 16:11). Do not read the word as “fullness [sova]” but as seven [sheva].

verse.he: תּוֹדִיעֵנִי אֹרַח חַיִּים שֹׂבַע שְׂמָחוֹת אֶת־פָּנֶיךָ נְעִמוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶצַח׃ {פ}
verse.en:
You will teach me the path of life.
In Your presence is perfect joy;
delights are ever in Your right hand.

messages.text: This indicates that the “sweet harp” (see Psalms 81:3) played in the presence of God, i.e., in the Temple, has seven strings.

And the harp that will be played in the days of the Messiah will have eight strings, as it is stated: “For the Leader, on the eighth: A Psalm of David” (Psalms 12:1). This indicates that the psalms that will be recited in the time of the Messiah, son of David, will be played on the eighth string that will be added to the harp.

verse.en: For the leader; on the sheminith. A psalm of David.

messages.text: And the harp that will be played in the World-to-Come will have ten strings, as it is stated: “A Psalm, a song. For the Shabbat…With an instrument of ten strings and with the lyre, with a solemn sound upon the harp” (Psalms 92:1–4).

verse.he: מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת׃ טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַיהֹוָה וּלְזַמֵּר לְשִׁמְךָ עֶלְיוֹן׃ לְהַגִּיד בַּבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת׃ עֲלֵי־עָשׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי־נָבֶל עֲלֵי הִגָּיוֹן בְּכִנּוֹר׃
verse.en:
A psalm. A song; for the sabbath day. It is good to praise GOD,
to sing hymns to Your name, O Most High, To proclaim Your steadfast love at daybreak,
Your faithfulness each night With a ten-stringed harp,
with voice and lyre together.

notes.he: כלומר היה [עשור] בנימין:
notes.en: “With an instrument of ten strings [asor] and with the lyre [nevel]”: that is, it had [ten] strings.

messages.text: This indicates that in the World-to-Come, which is comparable to Shabbat, songs of praise to God will be played on a ten-stringed instrument, identified here as both a lyre and a harp.
And similarly, another verse states: “Give thanks unto the Lord with the harp; sing praises unto Him with the lyre of ten strings. Sing unto Him a new song” (Psalms 33:2–3),

verse.he: הוֹדוּ לַיהֹוָה בְּכִנּוֹר בְּנֵבֶל עָשׂוֹר זַמְּרוּ־לוֹ׃ שִׁירוּ־לוֹ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ הֵיטִיבוּ נַגֵּן בִּתְרוּעָה׃
verse.en:
Praise GOD with the lyre;
with the ten-stringed harp sing out; sing [God] a new song;
play sweetly with shouts of joy.

notes.he: של עשר נימין. ולעולם הבא משתעי מדכתיב שיר חדש לשון זכר דשירות העולם הזה לשון נקבה כדאמר במכילת' כשם שנקבה זו יולדת כך תשועות הללו סופן לילד צרות אבל שיר של עולם הבא ל' זכר שאינו יולד:
notes.en: Gemara. With the ten-stringed lyre [nevel asor]: of ten strings. And it is speaking of the World-to-Come, since it is written “a new song [shir ḥadash],” in the masculine form; for the songs of this world are in the feminine form [shira], as is said in the Mekhilta: just as a female gives birth, so these salvations are destined to give birth to troubles. But the song of the World-to-Come is in the masculine form, as it does not give birth.

messages.text: which is referring to the new song that will be sung only in the World-to-Come. This proof in support of Rabbi Yehuda’s claim that the harp used in the World-to-Come will have ten strings is from a verse that is referring to a ten-stringed lyre, which shows that according to Rabbi Yehuda, the lyre and harp are the same instrument. Therefore, his opinion apparently contradicts the mishna.

notes.he: ואומר הודו לה' בכנור בנבל עשור ולא כתיב ובנבל אלמא [קסבר] דחד הוא:
notes.en: And it says: “Give thanks unto the Lord with the harp; with the lyre of ten strings,” and it is not written “and with the lyre”; evidently [he holds] that they are one.

messages.text: You may even say the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as even he agrees that the harp and lyre are essentially two different instruments.
messages.quote: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda

notes.he: מדמפיק ר' יהודה כנור בנבל עשור אלמא כנור היינו נבל:
notes.en: Since Rabbi Yehuda derives the harp [kinor] from “the ten-stringed lyre [nevel asor],” evidently a harp is a lyre.

messages.text: But in the World-to-Come, since the strings of the harp will be increased, its sound will be increased like that of the lyre, and therefore he calls the harp a lyre.

notes.he: ונבל עשוי כמפוח של נפחים ומוציא קול ע"י רוח:
notes.en: Its sound is increased like a lyre: and a lyre [nevel] is made like a blacksmith’s bellows and produces its sound by means of air.

notes.he: בכנור לעולם הבא:
notes.en: Since its strings are increased: of the harp in the World-to-Come.

notes.he: ונפיש קליה כי נבל באותו נבל שמכוסה בעור הכרס קרי ליה נבל:
notes.en: Its sound is increased like a lyre: that lyre which is covered with the skin of the belly; he calls it a lyre.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: The minors are not tallied in the minimum total of twelve Levites…and they were called cadets [tzoarei] of the Levites.
messages.quote: are not tallied in the minimum total

messages.text: And they were called the helpers [soadei] of the Levites.

notes.he: עוזרי:
notes.en: And soadei: helpers.

notes.he: מסייעי הלוים בשיר:
notes.en: And helpers [soadei] of the Levites: those who assist the Levites in the song.

messages.text: And the tanna of our mishna, why is he referring to them as tzoarei?

Since these minors had high voices and those adults had deep voices, and these minors would sing in a high voice [mekateti], and those adults could not sing in such a high voice, they were called tzoarei, as they caused the adult Levites anguish [tza’ar] due to the fact that they could not produce the same pleasant sounds as the minors.

notes.he: לויים עבו קלייהו. קטנים קטין קלייהו דק קולם:
notes.en: The Levites’ voices are thick. The minors’ voices are thin: their voice is fine.

notes.he: כלומר מקטינין ועושים קולם דק דק ויפה ומצערין הלוים שאין יכולים לבסם קולם כמותן:
notes.en: Mekatetei: that is, they make [their voice] small, making it very fine and beautiful; and they cause the Levites anguish, since they cannot sweeten their voice like theirs.

notes.he: הקטנים מקטטין מקטינין קולן שקולן דק והני הגדולים לא מקטטי קולן שקולן עבה משום הכי קרי להו צעירי הלוים]:
notes.en: These: the minors are mekatetei, they make their voices small, for their voice is fine; and those, the adults, do not make their voices small, for their voice is thick. Therefore they call them tze’irei [the young ones] of the Levites.] [So Rabbeinu Gershom’s text, reading “tze’irei” rather than “tzoarei.”]

notes.he: הדרן עלך אין נערכין
notes.en: We will return to you, Ein Ne’erakhin.

messages.text: הדרן עלך אין נערכין · Hadran alakh Ein Ne’erakhin: we will return to you, chapter 2, “One Is Not Valuated [for Less Than a Sela].”
Chapter 3 · יש בערכין · Yesh BaArakhin: halakhot that are lenient and stringent, in valuations, an ancestral field, the forewarned ox that killed a slave, and the rapist, the seducer and the defamer.
Mishna
There are halakhot with regard to valuations that are lenient and others that are stringent;

notes.he: מתני' להקל:
notes.en: Mishna. To be lenient: [heading; explained with the next comment].

notes.he: שהמעריך הכעור שבישראל אפי' אינו שוה אלא ה' סלעים נותן נ' סלעים מן עשרים עד בן ס':
notes.en: To be stringent: for one who valuates the most unsightly among the Jewish people, even if he is worth only five sela, gives fifty sela, [for one] from twenty until sixty years old.

notes.he: יש בערכין:
notes.en: Yesh BaArakhin [Tosafot’s heading for the new chapter, with no comment of its own here].

messages.text: and there are halakhot with regard to an ancestral field that are lenient and others that are stringent;

notes.he: במקדיש שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: With regard to an ancestral field: with regard to one who consecrates an ancestral field.

notes.dh: (שייך לדף י"ד ע"א) מה בין שדה מקנה לשדה אחוזה כו'
notes.he: והוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר חילוק אחר בין שדה אחוזה לשדה מקנה שבשדה אחוזה אם הקדישו וגאלו אחר מתחלק לכהנים ביובל ובשדה מקנה אם הקדישו וגאלו אחר חוזר לבעלים ביובל ולא נחת לפרושי אלא חילוק דשייך כשהוא עצמו פודהו:
notes.en: (This belongs to 14a.) What is the difference between a purchased field and an ancestral field, etc.: And similarly, it could have stated another difference between an ancestral field and a purchased field: with an ancestral field, if he consecrated it and another redeemed it, it is divided among the priests at the Jubilee; and with a purchased field, if he consecrated it and another redeemed it, it returns to the [original] owners at the Jubilee. But it chose to explain only a difference that applies when he himself redeems it.

notes.he: אחד המקדיש שדהו] שבחולת המחוז היינו שדה שסמוכה למחוז העיר שדורכין אותה בני אדם ועוד כיון שסמוכה לעיר ועומדת בקמותיה רואין אותה (הכל) [בני אדם] ונותנין בה עין הרע ואינה עושה פירות כל כך:
notes.en: One who consecrates his field] in the sandy area of Meḥoza [this explains the continuation of the mishna on 14a]: that is, a field near the city’s outskirts, which people tread upon; and moreover, since it is near the city and stands with its standing grain, [people] see it and cast an evil eye upon it, and it does not produce so much fruit.

messages.text: and there are halakhot with regard to a forewarned ox that killed a Canaanite slave that are lenient and others that are stringent; and there are halakhot with regard to a rapist, and a seducer, and a defamer that are lenient and others that are stringent.

There are halakhot with regard to valuations that are lenient and others that are stringent; how so? Both in the case of one who took a vow of valuation to donate the fixed value of the most attractive among the Jewish people and in the case of one who took a vow of valuation to donate the fixed value of the most unsightly among the Jewish people, he gives the fixed payment of fifty sela, shekels, to the Temple treasury (see Leviticus 27:3).

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight;

notes.he: שוה מאה מנה אין נותן אלא נ' סלע:
notes.en: The most attractive among the Jewish people: who is worth a hundred maneh; he gives only fifty sela.

notes.he: שאמר ערך פלוני עלי:
notes.en: Who took a vow of valuation: who said: The valuation of so-and-so is upon me.

notes.he: שאם העריך את הנאה שבישראל אינו נותן אלא נ' סלע:
notes.en: Yesh BaArakhin [to be lenient and to be stringent: that if he valuated the most attractive among the Jewish people, he gives only fifty sela.

notes.he: שאם העריך את הכעור שבישראל נותן נמי נ' סלע:
notes.en: And to be stringent: that if he valuated the most unsightly among the Jewish people, he also gives fifty sela.

messages.text: And if one said: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of another to the Temple treasury, he gives the price for that person if sold as a slave, a sum that can be more or less than fifty shekels.
Gemara

The Gemara infers from this that if the vow of valuation referred to a Jew, yes, he pays the fixed value; but if one took a vow of valuation to donate the fixed value of gentiles, he does not pay the fixed value.
messages.quote: There are halakhot with regard to valuations that are lenient and others that are stringent; how so? Both in the case of one who took a vow of valuation

notes.he: שאם אמר ישראל ערך עובד כוכבים פלוני עלי לא אמר כלום דעובד כוכבים אינו נערך:
notes.en: Gemara. With regard to gentiles, no: that if a Jew said, The valuation of so-and-so the gentile is upon me, he has said nothing, since a gentile is not valuated.

notes.he: כלומר את הנאה שבישראל קתני ולא תנא את הנאה שבעובד כוכבים (אפילו עובד כוכבים) לימא מתני' כו':

He is valuated in a case where a Jew says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the fixed value of this gentile; but a gentile does not take a vow of valuation to donate his fixed value or the value of others.

notes.he: טעמא מפרש בפ"ק (לעיל ערכין דף ה:):
notes.en: Is valuated but does not take a vow of valuation: the reason is explained in the first chapter (above, Arakhin 5b).
